# Groth16 fixtures

Deterministic Groth16 test fixtures for the **mul-circuit** (proves
`a * b == c`) in three formats. Regenerated by the round-trip test in
`crates/mosaic-serde/tests/groth16_roundtrip.rs`.

## Layout

```
groth16/
└── mul-circuit/
    ├── snarkjs/                 # snarkjs JSON format
    │   ├── proof.json
    │   ├── verification_key.json
    │   └── public.json
    ├── arkworks/                # arkworks CanonicalSerialize uncompressed
    │   ├── proof.bin            # 256 B — matches wire size of canonical
    │   ├── vk.bin               # 584 B — canonical + 8B vec-len prefix
    │   └── public_inputs.bin    # 40 B — canonical + 8B vec-len prefix
    └── canonical/               # Mosaic canonical wire format
        ├── proof.bin            # 256 B — exact on-chain bytes
        ├── vk.bin               # 576 B
        └── public_inputs.bin    # 32 B
```

## Witness

```
a = 7
b = 6
c = a * b = 42
```

`c` is the single public input; `a` and `b` are private witnesses.

## Reproducibility

The fixtures are produced deterministically from two RNG seeds:
- Setup RNG seed:  `2026_04_20`
- Prove RNG seed:  `2026_04_21`

Both seeds are literal constants in the test. Any change to the seeds,
the arkworks version, or the circuit synthesis rewrites the fixtures
and fails the `committed_fixtures_match_regenerated_bytes` test until
the corpus is re-committed.

## Regenerating

```bash
MOSAIC_REGEN_FIXTURES=1 cargo test -p mosaic-serde \
    --features host-backend --test groth16_roundtrip
```

Commit the regenerated files and bump this README if the seeds changed.

## What the tests assert

| Test | Assertion |
|---|---|
| `roundtrip_arkworks_and_snarkjs_produce_equal_canonical_bytes` | Direct-encode, arkworks-decode, and snarkjs-decode paths all produce byte-equal canonical bytes, and those bytes verify via `mosaic-groth16` host backend. |
| `committed_fixtures_match_regenerated_bytes` | Bytes written to disk at the last regen match what the test would produce today. Catches drift. |
| `tampered_proof_byte_is_rejected` | Flipping a single bit in `proof.a.x` makes the verifier reject. |
| `wrong_public_input_is_rejected` | `c + 1` instead of `c` → verifier rejects. |

## Sizes

| Artifact | Canonical | Arkworks | Snarkjs JSON |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proof | 256 B | 256 B | ~720 B |
| VK | 576 B | 584 B | ~1.6 KB |
| Public inputs | 32 B | 40 B | ~6 B |

Arkworks adds 8 B Vec-length prefixes; snarkjs JSON is decimal-string
encoded so it's the largest. Mosaic canonical is the tightest wire
format because it's exactly what the on-chain syscalls consume.

## Why a synthetic circuit instead of a real Circom compile?

For phase 1 we generate the proof programmatically via arkworks to keep
the fixture pipeline hermetic (no Node / Circom / snarkjs CLI required).
The round-trip test proves the snarkjs adapter works against JSON
equivalent to what Circom+snarkjs would emit.

Issue [#24](https://github.com/wienerlabs/mosaic/issues/24) tracks adding
real Circom-sourced fixtures once the end-to-end tutorial lands.
